toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Analyzer B most likely had one chance QC outlier (or a one-off sampling glitch), not a real fault. The repeat passed straight away. QC ran on schedule with no other rule violations. Level 2 QC averages are unchanged since the lot change. Analyzer A, on the old lot, agreed with B on 43 retested samples within 0.02 mmol/L on average. B's patient median is stable. So the lot change, skipped QC and a systematic fault are all unsupported. A one-in-300 flag is expected about once or twice a month.

Ward 6's high potassiums are split evenly between A and B. Most of them had long transport times since the tube station failed on 10 Nov. Renal overflow patients are another possible factor. The tube delay is a plausible cause but not proven, because no repeat samples were taken.

I'd sign off: return B to service, close the 186-result review with no amendments, and don't recall, quarantine the lot or widen limits. Don't label the cause as a confirmed sampling disturbance. Optionally add extra Level 2 QC for a week. Ask Ward 6 to recollect samples, and get the tube fixed. I'm moderately confident, around 70%.
